definitions.explanation: A narrow street or alley behind or between buildings, often in older urban areas.

examples.japanese: {路地裏|ろじうら}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: To go into a back alley.

examples.japanese: {路地裏|ろじうら}の{居酒屋|いざかや}を{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: I found a pub in a back alley.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}の{路地裏|ろじうら}には{昔|むかし}ながらの{店|みせ}が{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Old-fashioned shops line the back alleys of this town.

notes:
Composed of {路地|ろじ} (alley) + {裏|うら} (behind, back). Narrow passages behind or between buildings in older urban areas.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {路地裏|ろじうら}の{店|みせ}: a back-alley shop
- {路地裏|ろじうら}に{入|はい}る: to go into a back alley
- {路地裏|ろじうら}を{歩|ある}く: to walk through back alleys

CULTURAL NOTE:
{路地裏|ろじうら} often has positive connotations in Japanese — hidden gem restaurants, nostalgic old-town charm, and authentic local atmosphere. Many food and travel guides specifically recommend {路地裏|ろじうら} spots.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {路地|ろじ}: alley, lane (narrower term)
- {裏通|うらどお}り: back street (slightly wider)
- {横丁|よこちょう}: side street (often a row of small shops/bars)
